questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using the **BODMAS** rule by prioritising brackets and multiplication.

Calculate **Bracket**: (41 + 23) = 64.

Calculate **Multiplication**: 64 × 2 = 128.

Final expression: 56 + 74 − 52 + 128 − 96 = 110.

**∴ The correct answer is 110.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 56 + 74 − 52 + (41 + 23) × 2 − 96

**Rule Used:** **BODMAS** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 56 + 74 − 52 + (64) × 2 − 96

⇒ 56 + 74 − 52 + 128 − 96

⇒ (56 + 74 + 128) − (52 + 96)

⇒ 258 − 148

⇒ 110

**∴ The correct answer is 110.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: **Brackets** (), **Of** (orders like powers/roots), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Left-to-Right Rule

When operators of the same priority level appear (like + and −), solve the expression from **left to right** to maintain accuracy.

questions.question: 72 + 38 - (96 ÷ 12) + 29 of 2 - 14 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the expression using the **BODMAS** rule by identifying operations in order.

72 + 38 − (**96 ÷ 12**) + **29 of 2** − 14

⇒ 72 + 38 − 8 + 58 − 14

⇒ 110 + 50 − 14

⇒ 160 − 14 = 146

**∴ The correct answer is 146.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

72 + 38 − (96 ÷ 12) + 29 of 2 − 14

**Formula Used:**

Apply the **VBODMAS** rule (Vinculum, Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

**Calculations:**

⇒ 72 + 38 − 8 + 29 of 2 − 14 (Solving **Bracket**: 96 ÷ 12 = 8)

⇒ 72 + 38 − 8 + 58 − 14 (Solving **Of**: 29 × 2 = 58)

⇒ 110 − 8 + 58 − 14 (Solving **Addition**: 72 + 38 = 110)

⇒ 102 + 58 − 14 (Solving **Subtraction**: 110 − 8 = 102)

⇒ 160 − 14 (Solving **Addition**: 102 + 58 = 160)

⇒ 146 (Solving **Subtraction**: 160 − 14 = 146)

**∴ The correct answer is 146.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

The order of priority is **Vinculum** (bar), **Brackets** (), **Of** (multiplication), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

'Of' Operator

The 'of' operator is treated as multiplication but must be performed before **Division** and **Multiplication** according to standard mathematical hierarchy.

Left-to-Right Rule

When operations of the same priority (like Addition and Subtraction) appear, it is best to solve them from **left to right** to avoid confusion.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Separate **Whole Numbers** and **Fractions**: (7 + 9 − 5) + (2/7 + 1/3 − 3/4)

Integer part: 11

Fraction part: LCM(7, 3, 4) = 84

Fractional sum: (24 + 28 − 63) / 84 = −11/84

Combine: 11 − 11/84 = 10 + (1 − 11/84) = 10(73/84)

**∴ The correct answer is 10(73/84).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 7(2/7) + 9(1/3) − 5(3/4)

**Method:** Mixed fraction decomposition into **Integer** and **Proper Fraction**.

⇒ (7 + 2/7) + (9 + 1/3) − (5 + 3/4) ⇒ (7 + 9 − 5) + (2/7 + 1/3 − 3/4) ⇒ 11 + [(2 × 12 + 1 × 28 − 3 × 21) / 84] ⇒ 11 + [(24 + 28 − 63) / 84] ⇒ 11 + [−11 / 84] ⇒ 11 − 11/84 ⇒ 10 + 1 − 11/84 ⇒ 10 + (84 − 11) / 84 ⇒ 10 + 73/84 ⇒ 10(73/84)

**∴ The correct answer is 10(73/84).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixed Fractions

A **mixed fraction** is the sum of a non-zero **integer** and a **proper fraction**. For any mixed fraction A(b/c), it is calculated as (A × c + b) / c.

LCM of Denominators

When performing **addition** or **subtraction** of fractions, a common denominator must be established using the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given denominators.

Negative Fractional Parts

If the sum of fractional parts is negative, borrow 1 from the **integer part** (1 = c/c) to make the resulting fractional part positive.

questions.question: frac{sqrt{0.09}}{0.6} times (0.4)/(sqrt{0.36)} times (1.8)/(sqrt{0.36)} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **square roots** first: √0.09 = 0.3 and √0.36 = 0.6.

Substitute back: (0.3/0.6) × (0.4/0.6) × (1.8/0.6).

Simplify each fraction: (1/2) × (2/3) × 3.

Multiply the simplified values: 0.5 × 2 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (√0.09/0.6) × (0.4/√0.36) × (1.8/√0.36)

**Method:** **BODMAS** and **Square Root** simplification

⇒ Step 1: Find the **square roots** of the decimals.

⇒ √0.09 = √(9/100) = 3/10 = 0.3

⇒ √0.36 = √(36/100) = 6/10 = 0.6

⇒ Step 2: Substitute values into the expression.

⇒ Result = (0.3/0.6) × (0.4/0.6) × (1.8/0.6)

⇒ Step 3: Simplify the **ratios**.

⇒ Result = (1/2) × (2/3) × 3

⇒ Result = (1/2) × 2 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Decimals

To find the **square root** of a decimal, express it as a fraction (e.g., 0.09 = 9/100) and then take the square root of both numerator and denominator.

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the **BODMAS** order: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division and Multiplication (left to right), and Addition and Subtraction.

Fraction Simplification

When dealing with **decimal fractions**, you can remove decimals by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 10ⁿ, where n is the number of decimal places.

questions.question: sqrt{18² + 8 times 8 - 5 times 22 + 11} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the expression under the square root by calculating the **square** and products first.

18² = 324, 8 × 8 = 64, and 5 × 22 = 110.

Combine the results: 324 + 64 − 110 + 11 = 289.

The **square root** of 289 is 17.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √(18² + 8 × 8 − 5 × 22 + 11)

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ √(324 + 64 − 110 + 11)

⇒ √(388 − 110 + 11)

⇒ √(278 + 11)

⇒ √289

⇒ 17

**∴ The correct answer is 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The **BODMAS** acronym defines the correct sequence for solving mathematical operations: **Brackets**, **Orders** (powers/roots), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Perfect Squares

Memorizing **perfect squares** from 1 to 30 (e.g., 17² = 289, 18² = 324) is crucial for improving speed in **simplification** and **quantitative aptitude** sections.

Square Root Calculation

The **square root** (√) is the inverse operation of squaring a number; if x² = y, then √y = x.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 216 square cm. One of the diagonal is 18 cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Second **diagonal** (d₂) = (2 × 216) ÷ 18 = 24 cm. Half-diagonals are 9 cm and 12 cm. Using the **Pythagorean triplet** (3, 4, 5) scaled by 3 → (9, 12, 15). Therefore, the **side** of the **rhombus** = 15 cm. **Perimeter** = 4 × 15 = 60 cm. **∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 384 square cm. One of the diagonal is 24 cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area** of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

384 = (1/2) × 24 × d₂ ⇒ d₂ = 32 cm.

Half-diagonals are 12 and 16. Using **Pythagorean Triplet** (3, 4, 5) scaled by 4 ⇒ Side = 20 cm.

**Perimeter** = 4 × Side = 4 × 20 = 80 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Area = 384 cm², Diagonal 1 (d₁) = 24 cm.

**Formula Used:**

1. Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

2. Side (a) = √((d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²)

3. Perimeter = 4a

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03115d0867086e8bc0313ed97b811c7fdb58b3614719b63b939152aa140f6d12.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 24 × d₂

⇒ 384 = 12 × d₂

⇒ d₂ = 384 ÷ 12 = 32 cm

⇒ Side a = √((24/2)² + (32/2)²)

⇒ Side a = √(12² + 16²)

⇒ Side a = √(144 + 256) = √400

⇒ Side a = 20 cm

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 20 = 80 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 80 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all sides equal. Its **diagonals bisect** each other at 90°.

Relation between Side and Diagonals

The side 'a' and diagonals 'd₁' and 'd₂' are related by the equation 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Area of Rhombus

Area can also be calculated as **Base × Height** if the altitude is known.

questions.question: Least Common Multiple of A and B is 20. Least Common Multiple of C and D is 30. What is the Least Common Multiple of A, B, C and D?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** follows the **associative property**, which states that LCM(A, B, C, D) = LCM[LCM(A, B), LCM(C, D)].

⇒ Given LCM(A, B) = 20 and LCM(C, D) = 30.

⇒ Required LCM = LCM(20, 30).

⇒ The smallest number divisible by both 20 and 30 is 60.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of A and B = 20

LCM of C and D = 30

**Formula Used:**

LCM(a, b, c, d) = LCM(LCM(a, b), LCM(c, d))

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33f6458cafa37d89f0206f2e76b7ecc378829687d7ee56fbacdc68d4ba53ce37.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ We need to find the **LCM of 20 and 30**.

⇒ **Prime factorization** of 20 = 2 × 2 × 5 = 2² × 5

⇒ **Prime factorization** of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM is the product of the **highest powers** of all prime factors involved.

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Associative Property of LCM

The LCM of a set of numbers can be found by grouping them: LCM(a, b, c) = LCM(a, LCM(b, c)).

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

LCM of Fractions

LCM of (a/b, c/d) = LCM of numerators (a, c) ÷ HCF of denominators (b, d).

questions.question: The Least Common Multiple of two numbers is 90. Which of the following can be the Highest Common Factor of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of any set of numbers is always a **factor** of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

Given **LCM** = 90, the potential **HCF** must divide 90 exactly without a remainder.

Checking options: 90 ÷ 28 (No) | 90 ÷ 24 (No) | 90 ÷ 36 (No) | 90 ÷ 15 = 6 (Yes).

Since only 15 is a **factor** of 90, it is the only possible **HCF**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**LCM** of two numbers = 90

**Formula/Property:**

For any two integers, **LCM** = **HCF** × k (where k is a positive integer representing the product of the non-common prime factors).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c7b2288e8f485bf17c61cbdfeed7e25bd9ed4829b58eadd68dff0c7f5210377.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **HCF** be 'h'. Then 90/h must be an integer.

⇒ Option 1: 90 ÷ 28 ≈ 3.21 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 2: 90 ÷ 24 = 3.75 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 3: 90 ÷ 36 = 2.5 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 4: 90 ÷ 15 = 6 (Integer)

⇒ Since 15 divides 90 perfectly, it can be the **HCF**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any two positive integers a and b: Product of numbers = **HCF**(a, b) × **LCM**(a, b).

HCF vs LCM Magnitude

The **HCF** is always less than or equal to the **LCM**. Specifically, **HCF** ≤ smaller number ≤ larger number ≤ **LCM**.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, their **HCF** is 1 and their **LCM** is simply the product of the two numbers.

Divisibility Rule

The **LCM** of a set of numbers is the smallest number that is **divisible** by all the numbers in that set.

questions.question: Cost price of an article is Rs. 480. The profit percentage is 10 percent. What is the value of profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find **10%** of any value, simply divide the number by **10** or shift the decimal point one place to the left.

Profit = 480 ÷ 10

Profit = Rs. 48

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the article = Rs. 480

**Profit Percentage** = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × Cost Price

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7025bd48585e9cf8bd0545cab0b45107b08c1eab675fcc89387f1e80683838db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = (10 ÷ 100) × 480

⇒ Profit = 0.1 × 480

⇒ Profit = Rs. 48

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price (SP) Calculation

The selling price is the sum of cost price and profit: SP = CP + Profit. In this case, SP = 480 + 48 = Rs. 528.

Loss Calculation

If the article is sold for less than the CP, a loss occurs. Loss = CP − SP. Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Direct SP Formula

To find SP directly when Profit% is known: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: If x percent of x is 225, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **x% of x = k**, the value of **x** is directly calculated as 10 × √k.

Here, k = 225.

⇒ x = 10 × √225

⇒ x = 10 × 15 = 150.

**∴ The correct answer is 150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The expression is **x percent of x** is equal to **225**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f3c950373d938a21f2127e8ff209ed6ab7e09982cbe941436f3fa1f9d93d73d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x ÷ 100) × x = 225

⇒ x² ÷ 100 = 225

⇒ x² = 225 × 100

⇒ x² = 22500

⇒ x = √22500

⇒ x = 150

**∴ The correct answer is 150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Percentage Formula

The percentage of a number is calculated as: Value = (Percentage × Total) ÷ 100.

Square Root Calculation

To find the value from its square, take the square root. For example, √(a × b) = √a × √b. Here, √22500 = √225 × √100 = 15 × 10 = 150.

Percentage and Fractions

Any percentage x% can be written as a fraction x/100 or a decimal 0.01x.

questions.question: A person has a loss of 25 percent on selling price. What will be his loss percentage on the cost price?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ 25% = 1/4 (fractional value). Loss is calculated on **Selling Price (SP)**, so let **SP = 4 units** and **Loss = 1 unit**. **Cost Price (CP)** = SP + Loss = 4 + 1 = 5 units. Loss percentage on **Cost Price** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100. **∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

questions.question: P got 25 percent less marks than Q. R got 40 percent less marks than Q. If sum of P, R and Q marks is 1410, then what is the difference between the marks of Q and R?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **P** : **Q** : **R** = 75 : 100 : 60 = 15 : 20 : 12

Total sum = 15 + 20 + 12 = 47 units

Given: 47 units = 1410 → 1 unit = 1410 ÷ 47 = 30

Difference (**Q** − **R**) = 20 − 12 = 8 units

Required difference = 8 × 30 = 240

**∴ The correct answer is 240 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**P** = **Q** − 25% of **Q**

**R** = **Q** − 40% of **Q**

Sum of **P**, **Q**, and **R** = 1410

**Formula Used:**

Total Marks = **P** + **Q** + **R**

Difference = **Q** − **R**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32d77e5de4d58976321dce578d677cae1690ad8e642e3f9f0791d335fd2a4ed8.png] 

⇒ Let the marks of **Q** be 100x.

⇒ Marks of **P** = 100x − 25% of 100x = 75x

⇒ Marks of **R** = 100x − 40% of 100x = 60x

⇒ Total Marks = 75x + 100x + 60x = 235x

⇒ 235x = 1410

⇒ x = 1410 ÷ 235 = 6

⇒ Difference between **Q** and **R** = 100x − 60x = 40x

⇒ Value of difference = 40 × 6 = 240

**∴ The correct answer is 240 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Rule

Always identify the **base value** (denominator) which typically follows keywords like 'than' or 'of' to set it as 100%.

Ratio Method for Percentages

Converting percentages to **fractions** (e.g., 25% = 1/4, 40% = 2/5) helps in establishing quick ratios between multiple entities.

Relative Percentage Change

If A is x% less than B, then the difference in their values is calculated as (x ÷ 100) × B.

questions.question: A, B and C together can complete a work in 18 days. A and B together can complete the same work in 24 days. C alone can complete the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of **C** = **Efficiency (A + B + C)** − **Efficiency (A + B)**

Total Work = LCM of (18, 24) = **72 units**

Efficiency of **(A + B + C)** = 72 ÷ 18 = **4 units/day**

Efficiency of **(A + B)** = 72 ÷ 24 = **3 units/day**

Efficiency of **C** = 4 − 3 = **1 unit/day**

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

questions.question: X alone can do a work in 12 days. Y alone can do the same work in 18 days. Z alone can do the same work in 36 days. All three together complete the work. questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 25 km/hr and 75 km/hr. Their lengths are 120 metres and 130 metres respectively. What will be the time (in seconds) taken by faster train to cross the slower train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in same direction = 75 − 25 = 50 km/hr.

**Total Distance** to cover = Sum of lengths = 120 + 130 = 250 m.

Time = **Distance** ÷ **Relative Speed**

Time = 250 ÷ (50 × 5/18) = 250 × 18 ÷ 250 = 18 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 sec.**

questions.question: Upstream speed and downstream speed of a boat is 15 km/hr and 25 km/hr respectively. What is the difference (in km/hr) between the speed of boat in still water and the speed of stream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By definition, the **Upstream speed** of a boat is the difference between its **speed in still water** and the **speed of the stream**.

The question asks for this exact difference: (Speed of boat in still water − Speed of stream).

Given **Upstream speed = 15 km/hr**.

Required difference = **15 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Downstream Speed (D)** = 25 km/hr

**Upstream Speed (U)** = 15 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Speed of boat in still water (x) = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed of stream (y) = (D − U) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f3ce0cd77c96fb884a335cac5a37768fc466d6b55274321cd84d91fbc59bac7e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of boat in still water (x) = (25 + 15) ÷ 2

⇒ x = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 km/hr

⇒ Speed of stream (y) = (25 − 15) ÷ 2

⇒ y = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 km/hr

⇒ Required Difference = x − y

⇒ Required Difference = 20 − 5 = 15 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

The speed of the boat when traveling with the current: **Speed in Still Water + Speed of Current**.

Upstream Speed

The speed of the boat when traveling against the current: **Speed in Still Water − Speed of Current**.

Speed of Boat Formula

Speed of boat in still water is calculated as **(Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2**.

Speed of Current Formula

Speed of stream or current is calculated as **(Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2**.

questions.question: When an article is sold for a discount of 40 percent, then there is a profit 50 percent. If the cost price of article is Rs. 1000, then what is the marked price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the ratio relation: **CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)**

**CP : MP** = (100 − 40) : (100 + 50) = 60 : 150 = 2 : 5

Given **CP** = 2 units = **Rs. 1000** ⇒ 1 unit = **Rs. 500**

**Marked Price (MP)** = 5 units = 5 × 500 = **Rs. 2500**

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Cost Price (CP)** = Rs. 1000, **Discount** = 40%, **Profit** = 50%.

**Formula Used:** **SP = CP × (1 + Profit/100)** and **SP = MP × (1 − Discount/100)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c6064469ca38a9c124741f7915600b8c6836b6aa2a23d74d55fc0c9f3ac8bda.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 + 50% of 1000

⇒ **SP** = 1000 + 500 = **Rs. 1500**

⇒ According to discount, **SP** = **MP** × (100 − 40)/100

⇒ 1500 = **MP** × 0.6

⇒ **MP** = 1500 ÷ 0.6 = **Rs. 2500**

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between MP and CP

A very useful direct relation is **MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%)**. This eliminates the need to calculate **SP** separately.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is **(d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100)%**.

Markup Percentage

The percentage by which **Marked Price** is higher than **Cost Price** is **Markup% = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100**.

questions.question: An article is sold for 25 percent loss. The value of discount given is (5/9) of the selling price. What is the marked price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 4 units. For 25% **Loss**, **Selling Price (SP)** = 3 units.

**Discount** = (5/9) × SP = (5/9) × 3 = 5/3 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = SP + Discount = 3 + 5/3 = 14/3 units.

Ratio of MP to CP = (14/3) ÷ 4 = 14/12 = 7/6.

**∴ The correct answer is (7/6) of cost price.**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 1000. It is sold at a discount of 30 percent. If the cost price of the article is Rs. 520, then what is the value of profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Selling Price (SP)** = 70% of **Marked Price (MP)**

⇒ **SP** = 0.70 × 1000 = 700

**Profit** = **SP** − **Cost Price (CP)**

⇒ **Profit** = 700 − 520 = 180

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. 1000

**Discount** = 30%

**Cost Price (CP)** = Rs. 520

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e07540bfecc3a07666d2b1e0a654f81b6b36ff20c5408fbb63c359398feab55.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Marked Price (MP)** − **Discount**

**Profit** = **Selling Price (SP)** − **Cost Price (CP)**

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Discount Amount** = (30/100) × 1000 = Rs. 300

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 − 300 = Rs. 700

⇒ **Profit** = 700 − 520

⇒ **Profit** = Rs. 180

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage

Profit % = (**Profit** ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100. It measures the gain relative to the investment.

Discount Percentage

Discount % = (**Discount** ÷ **Marked Price**) × 100. Discounts are always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

Relation between CP and MP

MP ÷ CP = (100 + **Profit%**) ÷ (100 − **Discount%**). This direct ratio is useful for finding mark-up percentages.
